senses.gloss: (b. h.) to place, pile, esp. to place the cooking vessel over or by the fire.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:10:2">Y. Sabb. I, end, 4ᵇ</cite> <he>השׁוֹפֵת את הקדירה וכ׳</he> if one sets a pot over coals (on the Sabbath), we must warn him &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Beitzah 4:5">Bets. IV, 5</cite> <he>לִשְׁפּוֹת וכ׳</he> to place a pot on them, v. <cite ref="N01233"><he>נָקַף</he> I</cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 84a:21">Ḥull. 84ᵃ</cite> <he>מאה מנה יִשְׁפְּתוּ וכ׳</he> if one possesses one hundred Maneh, he may have a pot put on the stove every day.
<cite ref="Sotah 11b:4">Sot. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>שׁוֹפְתוֹת שתי וכ׳</he> they put on two pots, one for hot water, and one with fish; <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 1">Ex. R. s. 1</cite>.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 22">Midr. Till. to Ps. XXII, 16</cite> <he>הייתי דומה … שׁוֹפְתִין עליה</he> (not <cite ref="U00504"><he>שופכין</he></cite>) I was like a stove situate between two roads, on which the travellers do their cooking; ed. Bub. <he>ש׳ קרירותיהן עליה</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 687">Yalk. ib. 687</cite>; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 3:1">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. III, 1</cite> <he>שפת הימנה</he>, v. <cite ref="U01734"><he>שָׁפָה</he> I</cite>.]
